title: Radiologic Progression of Disease during Neoadjuvant Dostarlimab in Mismatch Repair-Deficient Lynch-Associated Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Resulting in Pathologic Complete Response: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade has demonstrated unprecedented activity in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), with high rates of clinical complete response and increasing adoption of organ-preservation strategies. However, response assessment during immunotherapy remains challenging as immune-mediated tumor regression may generate radiologic patterns that mimic persistent or progressive disease. CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 40-year-old woman with Lynch-associated dMMR mucinous LARC (cT4N+) treated with nine cycles of neoadjuvant dostarlimab. Early treatment was associated with rapid normalization of carcinoembryonic antigen and nodal regression. Nevertheless, magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated persistent bulky mass with new diffusion-restricted areas, and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography revealed intense metabolic uptake (SUVmax 14.7). A rising carbohydrate antigen 19-9 level further raised concern for residual viable tumor. Surgical exploration confirmed a large, firm pelvic mass with apparent infiltration of adjacent structures, leading to posterior pelvic exenteration. Unexpectedly, final pathologic examination revealed complete pathological response (ypT0 ypN0), with extensive fibrosis and acellular mucin pools and no viable tumor cells in 61 examined sections. CONCLUSION: Radiologic and metabolic findings suggestive of progression during neoadjuvant immunotherapy in dMMR LARC may not necessarily reflect treatment failure. This case underscores the limitations of conventional imaging in the context of immune-mediated tumor regression and highlights the importance of multidisciplinary evaluation when surgical decisions carry major oncologic and quality-of-life implications.

title: Primary Glomus Tumor of the Inferior Vena Cava Diagnosed by Endovascular Biopsy: A Rare Incidental Finding.
abstract: Glomus tumors are uncommon mesenchymal neoplasms with modified smooth muscle differentiation that classically arise in the subungual region but may occur at extradigital, visceral, and intravascular sites. Although primary intravascular glomus tumors have been reported, apparent primary origin within the inferior vena cava (IVC) represents an unusual presentation and must be distinguished from secondary caval involvement by an extravascular tumor. A 44-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis underwent musculoskeletal imaging for persistent right shoulder and upper back pain following a fall. Imaging incidentally demonstrated a 1.7-cm infrarenal IVC intraluminal abnormality initially interpreted as bland thrombus, while PET-CT showed no 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-avid malignancy. Endovascular evaluation demonstrated an obstructive intraluminal mass, and biopsy revealed uniform round-to-oval cells arranged around branching vascular channels. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong diffuse smooth muscle myosin heavy chain positivity with negative CAM 5.2 and chromogranin staining, supporting the diagnosis of glomus tumor. Subsequent surgical resection confirmed a 2.5-cm glomus tumor with smooth muscle actin (SMA) and caldesmon positivity and a low Ki-67 proliferative index (<1%). This case demonstrates the diagnostic challenge of an indeterminate intraluminal IVC lesion and emphasizes the importance of distinguishing apparent primary caval origin from secondary IVC tumor involvement. Endovascular tissue sampling can provide a minimally invasive means of establishing a diagnosis when imaging findings are inconclusive, and the integration of imaging, histomorphology, immunohistochemistry, and surgical pathology is essential for definitive classification.

title: Widespread Skeletal Fragility and Progressive Spinal Destruction Associated with Prolonged Tropomyosin Receptor Kinase Inhibitor Therapy: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) inhibitors have demonstrated remarkable efficacy in patients with NTRK fusion-positive malignancies; however, their long-term effects on skeletal health remain incompletely understood. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 65-year-old woman with an ETV6-NTRK3 fusion-positive gastrointestinal stromal tumor who achieved sustained disease control during prolonged TRK inhibitor therapy. During treatment, she developed progressive skeletal fragility characterized by multiple atraumatic fractures, delayed fracture healing, and progressive lumbar spinal destruction consistent with Charcot-like neuropathic arthropathy. Neurological deterioration, including loss of ambulation, resulted from structural spinal instability rather than direct neurotoxicity. Although initial imaging findings raised suspicion of metastatic disease, serial CT, MRI, and FDG-PET/CT examinations supported a nonmalignant skeletal process in the setting of continued oncologic remission. Following discontinuation of TRK inhibitor therapy, neurological symptoms stabilized and radiographic evidence of fracture healing was observed. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that TRK inhibitor-associated skeletal toxicity may represent an on-target effect related to disruption of neuro-skeletal interactions. Long-term monitoring of bone health may be warranted in patients receiving prolonged TRK inhibitor therapy.

title: CD10-Positive Extranodal Marginal Zone Lymphoma of the Thyroid Arising in Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Rare Diagnostic Challenge.
abstract: Patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) have an increased risk of developing primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL), with extranodal marginal zone lymphoma (ENMZL) representing a significant subset of these cases. We present the case of a 49-year-old woman with a history of HT, Sjögren's syndrome, and systemic lupus erythematosus who was incidentally found to have fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-avid thyroid nodules on PET-CT. Initial and repeat fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsies were either benign or indeterminate; however, flow cytometry revealed a small kappa-restricted B-cell population with dim CD10 expression. Given the persistent diagnostic uncertainty, the patient underwent total thyroidectomy, and histopathologic evaluation confirmed low-grade ENMZL with plasmacytic differentiation. Staging demonstrated localized stage IE disease. This case highlights important diagnostic challenges, including the potential for thyroid ENMZL to be missed on cytology despite ongoing clinical suspicion and the ability of rare aberrant CD10 expression in marginal zone lymphoma to mimic germinal-center-derived lymphomas.

title: Suspected Scrotal Metastasis Detected by 18F-FDG PET/CT in Recurrent Urachal Adenocarcinoma Associated with Subsequent High-Grade Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Urachal adenocarcinoma is a rare and aggressive malignancy arising from persistent urachal remnants and accounts for <1% of bladder cancers. Although the lungs, liver, lymph nodes, bone, and peritoneum are recognized sites of metastatic spread, involvement of scrotal structures is exceedingly uncommon. We report a case of recurrent urachal adenocarcinoma with an unusual pattern of metastatic dissemination identified on 18F-FDG PET/CT. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man underwent partial cystectomy with en bloc urachal resection and bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection for a moderately differentiated urachal adenocarcinoma arising from a persistent urachal remnant. Histopathology demonstrated a 6-cm tumor with perivesical extension and perineural invasion, while surgical margins and lymph nodes were negative. Approximately 6 months later, local recurrence was detected, and transurethral resection revealed high-grade urothelial carcinoma with supportive immunohistochemical findings. Restaging 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated a hypermetabolic recurrent bladder mass accompanied by pulmonary nodules suspicious for metastatic involvement, multiple intraperitoneal metastatic deposits, and an FDG-avid lesion within the right hemiscrotum highly suspicious for metastatic involvement. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the aggressive behavior and heterogeneous clinical course of urachal malignancies. In addition to confirming local recurrence, 18F-FDG PET/CT identified a lesion within the right hemiscrotum that was highly suspicious for metastatic involvement. Recognition of atypical metastatic patterns may improve disease staging and influence clinical management in patients with recurrent urachal carcinoma.

title: SDHB-Related Carney-Stratakis Syndrome Presenting with a Gastric Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor and a Clinically Suspected Paraganglioma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Carney-Stratakis syndrome (CSS) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary tumor-predisposition syndrome characterized by succinate dehydrogenase (SDH)-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and paragangliomas. These tumors typically arise in younger patients, may occur synchronously or metachronously, and often show limited sensitivity to conventional tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Given the potential for multifocal disease, recurrence, and familial involvement, accurate clinicopathological assessment, genetic evaluation, and long-term surveillance are essential. CASE PRESENTATION: A 36-year-old woman presented with a 7-month history of visual disturbance. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a hypervascular tumor extending from the left jugular foramen to the carotid sheath, raising clinical suspicion of a paraganglioma and prompting biochemical and functional imaging evaluation. Plasma noradrenaline and dopamine levels were elevated, whereas 123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scintigraphy showed no abnormal uptake. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography incidentally identified a gastric submucosal tumor. Because placement of a lumboperitoneal shunt for intracranial hypertension was expected to increase the risk of infection and complicate subsequent abdominal surgery, gastric resection was prioritized. Laparoscopic-endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) was selected to facilitate local resection of the tumor near the esophagogastric junction while preserving the cardia; an intraoperative perforation necessitated conversion to classical LECS, and complete macroscopic resection was achieved. Histopathological examination demonstrated a multinodular epithelioid GIST positive for KIT and DOG1, with loss of SDHB expression, indicating an SDH-deficient GIST. Germline testing identified a pathogenic SDHB variant, supporting the diagnosis of CSS in the context of the clinically suspected paraganglioma. The jugular foramen lesion, for which no histological diagnosis was obtained, was managed conservatively, and delayed shunt placement improved the visual symptoms. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of considering an SDH-related hereditary syndrome in a young patient with an SDH-deficient gastric GIST and a synchronous lesion clinically suggestive of paraganglioma. title: Synthesis and Preliminary Biological Evaluation of a Structurally Modified Niraparib-Based PARP-Targeted PET Tracer for Tumor Imaging.
abstract: Poly-(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) is highly expressed in various malignancies and represents an important therapeutic target. Noninvasive evaluation of PARP expression is therefore of potential clinical significance for patient stratification. In this study, we developed and evaluated [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827, a structurally modified PARP-targeted radiotracer derived from niraparib, featuring a two-carbon linker between the DOTA chelator and the pharmacophore. [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 demonstrated high uptake in MDA-MB-231 and OE-19 tumors with elevated PARP-1 expression, which was significantly reduced by blocking, supporting a PARP-related component of tumor accumulation. The tracer exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, including high hydrophilicity and predominantly renal clearance, resulting in low abdominal background activity. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging enabled clear tumor visualization with good contrast, supported by biodistribution findings. Preliminary clinical imaging further showed notable uptake in an esophageal cancer lesion, with immunohistochemical confirmation of PARP-1 expression in the biopsied tissue. These results suggest that [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 has potential as a PARP-targeted PET tracer for tumor imaging and merits further investigation in larger clinical cohorts.

title: Analytical Approaches for Detection, Characterization, and Environmental Significance of Suspended Particulate Matter in Aquatic Systems: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Suspended particulate matter (SPM) represents a component of aquatic systems, acting both as a carrier of contaminants and as a factor shaping ecosystem functioning. This review summarizes recent progress in methods for detecting and quantifying SPM in natural waters. Traditional gravimetric analysis provides a direct mass-based reference, while optical approaches such as turbidimetry and nephelometry enable rapid and automated assessments. Granulometric techniques, including sedimentation and laser diffraction, contribute to understanding particle size distribution and its role in transport, settling, and pollutant interactions. Chemical characterization, based on spectroscopic and spectrometric methods, identifies the composition of SPM and its association with heavy metals, organic pollutants, and microplastics. Particular attention is given to the ecological risks posed by fine particles, which remain suspended longer and enhance contaminant mobility. The review integrates findings from hydrochemistry, analytical chemistry, and environmental monitoring, outlining both the strengths and limitations of existing methods and highlighting directions for improving water-quality assessment and ecological risk evaluation.

title: Atypical Type A Thymoma Identified in Slowly Growing Pulmonary Metastases from Type A Thymoma: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Type A thymoma is generally considered a low-risk thymoma subtype with an excellent prognosis and low rates of distant metastasis. Atypical type A thymoma is a recently established entity characterized by more aggressive biological behavior despite retaining the morphology of conventional type A thymoma. Patients with primary conventional type A thymoma who subsequently develop recurrence with atypical histological features are extremely rare. CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old man was referred to our hospital due to gradual enlargement of bilateral pulmonary nodules. Seven years earlier, he had undergone complete resection of an anterior mediastinal tumor, which had been diagnosed as conventional type A thymoma. Retrospective review of preoperative computed tomography images revealed that small pulmonary nodules had already been present at the time of the initial surgery but had yet to be identified. The nodules enlarged slowly from 3 mm to 10 mm and from 3 mm to 7 mm over the 7-year period. Positron emission tomography showed no abnormal fluorodeoxyglucose uptake. After thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left lower lobe lesion, histopathological examination demonstrated pulmonary metastasis of type A thymoma with focal hypercellularity and increased mitotic activity, consistent with atypical type A thymoma. No necrosis was identified. The Ki-67 labeling indices of the primary and metastatic lesions were 7% and 20%, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that even apparently low-risk type A thymoma may exhibit indolent but metastatic behavior and may develop atypical histological features during a prolonged clinical course. Careful long-term surveillance and detailed pathological evaluation, including assessment of the Ki-67 labeling index, may be important in patients with type A thymoma.

title: A scientometric study on research trends and characteristics of lymph node metastasis in oral cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) is the most critical prognostic factor in oral cancer (OC) patients. The purpose of this study was to analyze the scientometric characteristics and research trends of LNM in OC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: All the papers on LNM in OC were comprehensively retrieved from the Scopus database. The years of publication were divided into before 2016 and after 2016 in the analysis of research trends. RESULTS: There were 946 papers on LNM in OC, with total citations of 21,154 and the h index of 70. The trend of clinical aspect including lymph node excision, lymphadenectomy, and sentinel lymph node biopsy has changed to early cancer, extranodal extension, chemoradiotherapy, and distant metastasis after 2016. The trend of diagnostic aspect has highlighted depth of invasion, perineural invasion, deep learning, machine learning, nomogram, and diagnostic imaging by PET-CT, contrast enhancement, and radiomics. Moreover, the trend of laboratory investigation including immunoenzyme techniques, neoplasm proteins, and VEGF-C has changed to tumor microenvironment, tumor differentiation, and signal transduction after 2016. There have always been common keywords such as neck dissection, tongue tumor, metabolism, genetics, risk factor, tumor marker, cancer surgery, cisplatin, and cancer radiotherapy. CONCLUSION: This scientometric study for the first time elucidated the current scenario and research trends of LNM in OC, particularly the comprehensive identification and recognition of the important research topics concerned.

title: Isolated Thyroid Metastasis from High-Grade Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma After Radical Nephrectomy: A Case Report.
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Thyroid metastasis from clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is uncommon and may occur after radical nephrectomy despite no evidence of residual or metastatic disease at that time. Diagnosis can be challenging because imaging and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) may mimic benign or primary thyroid lesions. Case Presentation: A 55-year-old man underwent left radical nephrectomy for WHO/ISUP grade 3 ccRCC with focal grade 4 differentiation. Two years later, surveillance ultrasonography detected a suspicious lesion involving the thyroid isthmus and left lobe. FNA was interpreted as Bethesda II (benign), but metastatic ccRCC was subsequently confirmed after total thyroidectomy. Histopathology showed focal vascular and capsular invasion. Tumor reached the margin of the main thyroid specimen, whereas separately submitted perithyroidal soft tissue had tumor-free margins, resulting in a final R0 resection. The tumor was positive for CK8/18, PAX8, EMA, vimentin, and CD10 and negative for TTF-1, thyroglobulin, calcitonin, and CD5. Postoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT showed no additional metastatic disease. Conclusions: Benign thyroid cytology should be interpreted cautiously in patients with previous ccRCC when clinical or imaging findings remain suspicious. Diagnosis requires integration of oncological history, imaging, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry. Surgical resection may provide local disease control in selected patients, with surveillance.

title: Multiparametric imaging with dynamic 18 F-FDG PET shows increased breast glucose metabolism in patients with breast cancer.
abstract: PURPOSE: Multiparametric PET separates tracer signal into bound and free fractions via reconstructions that reflect the net trapping rate (Ki) and apparent distribution volume (DV). This study aimed to investigate differences in background parenchymal uptake (BPU) between patients with and without breast cancer using multiparametric PET and to evaluate differences in primary tumor uptake according to hormone receptor status. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included female patients (n = 48) with newly diagnosed breast cancer and 146 patients without breast cancer. Patients with breast cancer under or after treatment and patients with bilateral breast cancer were excluded. Enrolled patients underwent whole-body dynamic PET and three quantitative indices representing BPU (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax], Ki and DV) were calculated. The primary tumor uptake was calculated between estrogen- or progesterone-receptor-positive and -negative groups. RESULTS: The mean SUVmax, Ki and DV of breast cancer cases were 1.39 ± 0.352, 4.88 × 10 - 3 ± 1.61 × 10 - 3 and 24.2 ± 15.4 respectively, whereas in control cases, mean SUVmax, Ki and DV were 1.10 ± 0.320, 3.96 × 10 - 3 ± 1.25 × 10 - 3 and 17.1 ± 10.8 respectively (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004). The areas under the curve from the ROC analysis for breast cancer presence were calculated as 0.727, 0.681 and 0.653 respectively. In addition, age-stratified analysis showed that SUVmax and Ki were significantly higher in patients with breast cancer than in patients without breast cancer. Regarding the primary tumor uptake, Ki was significantly higher in the estrogen receptor-positive group. CONCLUSION: Multiparametric PET revealed that pure glucose metabolism is significantly elevated in the background mammary glands of patients with breast cancer, and the Ki in the primary tumor is associated with ER status. Dynamic PET imaging may be a useful imaging biomarker for the development of breast cancer.

title: Coupled sediment and microplastic fluxes revealed by check-dam sediment records.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as pervasive contaminants in terrestrial environments, yet their redistribution through erosion and accumulation within sediment-retention structures remains poorly quantified. This study quantified MPs in sediments retained behind check dams and examined their relationships with sediment storage and erosion-related sediment yield at the catchment scale. Twenty check dams in a semi-arid mountainous catchment in northeastern Iran were investigated. Sediment storage ranged from 531 to 9828 Mg (mean: 2683 Mg), while specific sediment yield ranged from 16.2 to 855.4 Mg km-2 yr-1 (mean: 247.1 Mg km-2 yr-1). MPs were detected in all sediment samples, with concentrations ranging from 800 to 5240 particles kg-1 dry sediment (mean: 2702 particles kg-1). Estimated MP inventories ranged from 9.0 × 108 to 2.4 × 1010 particles per check dam. Strong positive relationships were observed between specific sediment yield and estimated MP yield (r = 0.99, p < 0.01) and between accumulated sediment mass and estimated MP inventory (r = 0.80, p < 0.01), indicating a close association between sediment dynamics and MP redistribution. Fibrous MPs dominated the assemblage (86.6%), and the 500-1000 μm size class accounted for the largest proportion of detected particles (44.7%). Raman spectroscopy confirmed several polymer types within the analyzed subset. Overall, the findings show substantial accumulation of sediment-associated MPs behind check dams and indicate that erosion-driven sediment mobilization may represent an important pathway for MP redistribution in erosion-prone catchments. However, the persistence of this retention may depend on the stability of accumulated sediments, which can potentially be remobilized during high-energy hydrological events.

title: Radiopharmaceuticals for Melanoma Theranostics.
mesh: Humans; Melanoma; Radiopharmaceuticals; Theranostic Nanomedicine; Animals; Receptor, Melanocortin, Type 1
abstract: Malignant melanoma (MM) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and the eventual emergence of resistance to current BRAF/MEK and immune checkpoint inhibitors. To address these limitations, the theranostic strategy integrating diagnostic imaging with targeted radionuclide therapy to enable personalized treatment has gained significant traction. Current research primarily exploits the overexpression of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), very late antigen-4 (VLA-4), and melanin as primary molecular targets for radiopharmaceutical development. For MC1R, α-MSH peptide analogs have been engineered with β-emitters such as 177Lu and 90Y for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), as well as α-emitters like 225Ac and 212Pb (β- decay to 212Bi and then emit α particles) for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), showing high specificity and rapid clearance. Concurrently, VLA-4-targeted platforms utilizing high-affinity LLP2A ligands have been optimized through PEGylation and albumin-binding strategies to enhance bioavailability and tumor retention. Beyond these primary receptors, this review evaluates alternative strategies, including copper transporter (CTR1) targeting with 64CuCl2 and the use of gold nanocages for multimodal applications. Together, these advancements represent a critical shift toward image-guided, dosimetry-driven radionuclide therapies that may work synergistically with existing immunotherapies to improve survival in metastatic melanoma.

title: PET Imaging of Melanoma Using a Melanocortin 1 Receptor-Targeted Probe.
mesh: Receptor, Melanocortin, Type 1; Animals; Humans; Melanoma; Positron-Emission Tomography; alpha-MSH; Mice; Radiopharmaceuticals; Cell Line, Tumor; Gallium Radioisotopes; Tomography, Emission-Computed, Single-Photon
abstract: The melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) is overexpressed in more than 80% of melanoma cells but is expressed at low levels in normal tissues, making it an important target for melanoma imaging and therapy. Recently, MC1R has attracted the interest of numerous researchers as a target for melanoma. Radiolabeled alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) peptides bind specifically to MC1R and internalize into tumor cells, enabling melanoma diagnosis and therapy. Several radiolabeled α-MSH peptides have been developed. Among those, a cyclized α-MSH peptide produced via an alternative click chemistry cyclization strategy offers faster and more specific bindings to MC1R. It could be labeled with ²0³Pb/²¹²Pb (VMT01) for melanoma single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging and therapy and also could be labeled with 68Ga (VMT02) for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Preliminary clinical imaging showed highly sensitive and specific melanoma detection. This chapter describes the synthesis of VMT02 and PET/CT imaging procedures in both mouse models and patients.

title: First Presentation With Impending Cardiac Tamponade Leading to a New Diagnosis of Mediastinal Lymphoma: A Shared Learning Case on the Atypical Presentation of Pericardial Effusion and Cardiac Tamponade.
abstract: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency classically associated with Beck's triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; however, incomplete or atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 28-year-old woman who presented with progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, orthopnoea, peripheral oedema, fever, and fatigue. Examination revealed mild tachycardia, soft heart sounds, reduced basal air entry, and ankle oedema, while the patient remained normotensive. Initial investigations demonstrated cardiomegaly with pleural effusions on chest radiograph, low-voltage QRS complexes on electrocardiogram, and markedly raised inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography identified a large anterior mediastinal mass encasing the great vessels, a significant pericardial effusion with features of cardiac tamponade, and bilateral pleural effusions. Emergency pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate clinical improvement. Histopathological analysis confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma, most consistent with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with immunochemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic remission on end-of-treatment PET-CT. This case highlights the importance of recognising atypical presentations of cardiac tamponade and considering mediastinal malignancy in young patients presenting with unexplained cardiorespiratory symptoms.

title: Valorisation of PET-rich mixed plastic waste using a cascading concept involving selective ammonolysis and catalytic pyrolysis.
abstract: We report a cascading valorisation strategy for real polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-rich waste streams, combining selective ammonolysis of PET with catalytic pyrolysis of the non-PET residue. In this approach, PET-rich packaging waste is treated with ammonia in ethylene glycol to produce terephthaldiamide (TDA), while the remaining polyolefin (PO)-rich residue is subsequently upgraded to benzene, toluene, xylene (BTX), and light olefins over H-ZSM-5 catalyst. TDA is a valuable aromatic diamide and a potential precursor to p-phenylene diamine, a monomer used in the production of poly(p-phenyleneterephthalamide) (PPTA). For post-consumer PET trays, ammonolysis at 5 bar NH3, and 100 °C for 8 h, followed by a downstream separation procedure, resulted in an almost quantitative conversion of PET, yielding pure TDA as small crystals in 74 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content in the feed. The residue (mostly polyolefins) was converted to BTX (5 wt% on residue), and propene/butenes (19 wt%, on residue) using a catalytic in situ pyrolysis approach with H-ZSM-5 at 550 °C. The same strategy was applied to a PET-enriched, DKR-350 mixed-plastic packaging fraction, affording TDA in 71 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content, while catalytic pyrolysis of the residue produced BTX (3 wt%) and propene/isobutene (4 wt%) based on the residue. These results demonstrate that real PET-rich mixed plastic waste streams can be selectively upgraded into valuable aromatic diamide while retaining the non-PET fraction as a feedstock for petrochemical intermediates.

title: Unified alcoholysis-GC-MS/MS for simultaneous differentiation and quantification of polyester microplastics in water.
abstract: Environmental waters now carry complex mixtures of polyester microplastics that vary in origin and biodegradability, including fossil-based and biodegradable polyesters, yet no method can simultaneously distinguish and individually quantify them. We present a unified alcoholysis method coupled with GC-MS/MS to quantify four polyester microplastics (PEMPs) in a single workflow. By selectively cleaving ester bonds in an alcohol medium, the method converts polylactic acid, polyethylene terephthalate, polyhydroxybutyrate and polybutylene succinate into four distinct, stable monomers. These monomers are directly determined by GC-MS/MS without derivatization. Under unified conditions (190 °C, 5 h), depolymerization efficiencies range from 15% to 90%. We calibrate directly between polymer mass and monomer signal intensity. Detection limits are 0.0462 μg/L for polylactic acid (PLA), 0.103 μg/L for polyethylene terephthalate (PET), 2.92 μg/L for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), and 0.695 μg/L for polybutylene succinate (PBS). Spiked recoveries in lake water are 90-115%. In six lake samples, PLA constitutes over 75% of total PEMPs. This fingerprint points to consumer packaging as the dominant source. By circumventing particle morphology constraints and delivering polymer-specific mass concentrations, the method opens a direct route for source apportionment of coexisting fossil-based and biodegradable polyester microplastics.

title: GATA3-positive primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland with calcification: a case report.
abstract: Primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland (PDALG) is a rare epithelial malignancy of the ocular adnexa. A man in his 50s presented with painless swelling of the right upper eyelid and was found to have a right lacrimal gland mass with punctate hyperdense foci on computed tomography (CT) and low signal intensity on both T1- and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. Histopathology of the tumor revealed nest-like, cribriform, and tubular proliferation of atypical epithelial cells, with fibrotic and hyalinized stroma, comedo necrosis, and calcification. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for androgen receptor, HER2, and GATA3, while GCDFP-15 was negative. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography showed no systemic lesions, supporting the diagnosis of PDALG. Elastica van Gieson staining demonstrated venous invasion, and adjuvant radiotherapy was performed after complete excision. This case illustrates the diagnostic value of correlating punctate hyperdensity on CT with pathologic calcification and integrating GATA3/HER2 findings with the systemic exclusion of metastatic breast carcinoma. At 1 year of follow-up, no local recurrence or distant metastasis had been detected; however, given the potential for late metastasis in this pathology, long-term close observation is required.

title: Comparative diagnostic accuracy of PSMA-PET versus conventional imaging for Initial T/N/M staging of intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer: a patient-level paired bivariate meta-analysis.
mesh: Humans; Male; Prostatic Neoplasms; Neoplasm Staging; Positron-Emission Tomography; Tomography, X-Ray Computed; Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Antigens, Surface; Sensitivity and Specificity; Glutamate Carboxypeptidase II; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the patient-level diagnostic accuracy of PSMA-PET with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), computed tomography (CT), and bone scintigraphy (BS) for initial T, N, and M staging of newly diagnosed intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer using paired studies. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to December 1, 2025, for paired studies in which the same patients underwent PSMA-PET and conventional imaging, with histopathology or predefined composite criteria as the reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C. Pooled sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using bivariate composite-likelihood models. Modality effects were tested by meta-regression and likelihood ratio tests, and absolute between-modality differences with 95% CIs were estimated using the delta method. RESULTS: Forty-three studies including 4,023 patients were analyzed. For local T staging, PSMA-PET did not show uniform superiority over mpMRI. For extraprostatic extension, PSMA-PET/CT did not differ significantly from mpMRI in sensitivity (absolute difference, -7.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -16.1 to 0.9; p = 0.08) or specificity (-7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -14.7 to 0.8; p = 0.08); no significant differences were observed for seminal vesicle invasion. In an exploratory six-study comparison, PSMA-PET/MRI had higher sensitivity than mpMRI for extraprostatic extension (+ 12.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.9 to 22.2; p = 0.02). For regional lymph node staging, PSMA-PET/CT sensitivity was 69.3% (95% CI, 56.6-79.7) versus 45.3% (95% CI, 33.0-58.3) for mpMRI (difference, + 24.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.0-40.3; p = 0.009), whereas specificity did not differ (difference, + 3.2 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.6 to 11.8; p = 0.41). For bone metastasis staging, PSMA-PET had greater sensitivity than BS (95.8% [95% CI, 92.8-98.7] versus 76.2% [95% CI, 68.7-83.8]) and greater specificity (92.8% [95% CI, 89.9-95.7] versus 77.4% [95% CI, 71.3-83.5]; both p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: PSMA-PET/CT was more sensitive than mpMRI for regional lymph node staging, while specificity was comparable. PSMA-PET had greater sensitivity and specificity than bone scintigraphy for bone metastasis staging. For local T staging, PSMA-PET did not show uniform superiority over mpMRI.

title: AI-based automated body composition analysis from whole-body MRI and (PET-) CT: an intermodal comparison from same-day examinations.
mesh: Humans; Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Whole Body Imaging; Male; Female; Body Composition; Multiple Myeloma; Retrospective Studies; Aged; Middle Aged; Fluorodeoxyglucose F18
abstract: BACKGROUND: To determine intermodal agreement of AI-derived volumetric body composition metrics between [18 F]FDG-PET/CT-derived low-dose CT and whole-body MRI (wb-MRI). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed same-day whole-body low-dose CT, obtained from [18F]FDG-PET/CT, and wb-MRI from consecutive multiple myeloma patients from the prospective GMMG-HD7- and GMMG-HD8-/DSMM-XIX-trials. An automated deep learning pipeline based on the TotalSegmentator model, and its MRI variant were used to segment skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous- (SAT) and abdominal visceral adipose tissue (VAT) from CT and MRI, respectively. Volumetric measures and single-slice estimates were derived. Agreement between CT- and MRI-based metrics was assessed using Pearson r, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analyses. RESULTS: Forty-two multiple myeloma patients with same-day PET/CT and wb-MRI were included. For AI-based volumetric body composition metrics, CT and MRI demonstrated high agreement (ICC > 0.95) across all SM, SAT and VAT. However, Bland-Altmann plots revealed systematic modality-related differences between MRI and CT: both SM (bias: -2582 ml, p < 0.0001) and VAT (bias: -211 ml, p < 0.0001) were significantly lower when extracted from MRI compared to CT, while for SAT, the difference was not statistically significant (bias: -263 ml, p = 0.1629). For AI-based single slice analysis, agreement remained high for SAT and VAT (ICC > 0.97), while being lower for SM (ICC 0.87). Bland-Altman plots showed that SM was systematically and significantly lower when obtained from MRI than from CT (bias: -18.4cm2, p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: Automated body composition measures from (PET-)CT and wb-MRI are highly concordant but show consistent intermodal biases that should be considered when pooling multimodal data or applying modality-agnostic thresholds. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: Pancreatic Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm in a Carrier of a Reported Pathogenic BRCA2 Variant: Diagnostic Considerations and Management Using European and International Guidelines.
abstract: Pathogenic germline variants in BRCA2 are associated with increased susceptibility to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and may prompt pancreatic surveillance in selected high-risk individuals. Whether BRCA2 status increases the prevalence or alters the biological behavior of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) remains uncertain. We report a 71-year-old Latin American woman with a reported heterozygous pathogenic BRCA2 variant and a remote history of stage IA hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma. The original molecular genetics report was unavailable; therefore, the exact variant designation, testing platform, laboratory classification, and American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)/Association of Molecular Pathology (AMP) evidence could not be independently verified. In June 2025, during long-term oncologic follow-up, positron emission tomography-computed tomography incidentally identified a 21×21 mm pancreatic tail cyst. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) in July 2025 demonstrated a 22×20 mm cyst communicating with the main pancreatic duct (MPD), which measured 5 mm. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) demonstrated a 20×23 mm septated cyst without mural nodules or a solid component. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) was 21.4 U/mL. Cyst fluid glucose was 12 mg/dL, amylase 316 U/L, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) 247 ng/mL. Cytologic examination and an adequate cell-block specimen obtained by EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) demonstrated papillary mucinous epithelium with gastric-type features, favoring a low-grade IPMN. No immunohistochemical studies were performed, and the specimens were evaluated by a gastrointestinal pathologist. The case was reviewed by a multidisciplinary team in August 2025. The 5 mm MPD represented a relative indication for surgery under the 2018 European evidence-based guidelines and a worrisome feature under contemporary international criteria, but no absolute or high-risk indication for resection was identified. Surveillance was selected. Computed tomography (CT) in December 2025 showed a stable 22×20 mm cyst and a 5 mm MPD; serum CA 19-9 was 24.7 U/mL. In May 2026, the cyst measured 22×21 mm, and the MPD remained 5 mm. The patient remained clinically stable and asymptomatic without pancreatitis, obstructive jaundice, abdominal pain, weight loss, or other

title: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis mimicking seronegative rheumatoid arthritis: a case report of destructive erosive arthritis with partial response to Upadacitinib.
abstract: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis (MRH) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis that can mimic seronegative rheumatoid arthritis through destructive inflammatory arthritis and papulonodular skin lesions. We report a 44-year-old woman with progressive polyarthritis, purplish papulonodular lesions and destructive erosive disease of the hands and feet. Rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and antinuclear antibody were negative. Radiographs showed sharply demarcated erosions with prominent distal interphalangeal involvement, and skin biopsy confirmed MRH. Available malignancy screening, including oncology review, mammography, cervical screening and blood tests, was reassuring, although planned PET-CT was not completed due to loss to follow-up. Methotrexate and corticosteroids were not tolerated, certolizumab produced partial response, and upadacitinib led to modest cutaneous improvement but persistent active synovitis at four months. This case highlights MRH as a diagnostic mimic of seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and illustrates discordant treatment response to JAK inhibition.

title: Preoperative 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography maximum standardized uptake value is independently associated with overall survival in surgically resected undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) is the most common adult soft tissue sarcoma subtype, with heterogeneous survival despite optimal surgery. We evaluated whether the preoperative maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) is independently associated with overall survival (OS) in surgically resected UPS. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 79 patients with localized UPS who underwent curative resection between 2015 and 2023. Preoperative SUVmax, tumor grade (French Federation of Cancer Centers Sarcoma Group), tumor size, and Ki-67 index were assessed. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors for OS. RESULTS: The median age was 59 (range: 18-92) years; 53.2% of patients were male, and 59.5% of tumors were high grade. The median tumor size, Ki-67 index, and SUVmax were 60 mm, 60%, and 10, respectively. At a median follow-up of 58.9 months, median OS was not reached. In univariable analysis, tumor size (P = 0.007), Ki-67 (P = 0.001), SUVmax [hazard ratio: 1.08 per unit, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.04-1.10, P = 0.001], and high grade (P = 0.003) were associated with worse OS. In multivariable analysis, only SUVmax remained independently associated with OS (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.06 per unit, 95% CI: 1.02-1.10, P = 0.002), whereas grade, size, and Ki-67 did not retain significance. CONCLUSION: Preoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT SUVmax is independently associated with OS in surgically resected UPS and provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological parameters.

title: A Comprehensive Review of PET Chemical Depolymerization: Mechanisms, Catalyst Design, and Process Intensification Toward Closed-Loop Recycling.
abstract: The massive accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste necessitates efficient recycling technologies to mitigate environmental pollution. Chemical depolymerization converts PET into high-purity monomers, offering a promising route for closed-loop plastic circularity. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in catalytic PET depolymerization, emphasizing reaction mechanisms, catalyst design, and process intensification. We analyze major depolymerization routes, namely hydrolysis, methanolysis, glycolysis, and aminolysis while highlighting fundamental mechanistic insights such as nucleophilic transesterification and emerging β-cleavage pathways. Furthermore, we evaluate catalyst design principles for active sites (e.g., Brønsted and Lewis acids, bridged bimetallic centers, and defect-engineered structures) across various homogeneous and heterogeneous systems, including ionic liquids, metal-organic frameworks, and zeolites. Finally, we highlight recent progress in process intensification strategies, such as interfacial catalysis, microwave-assisted reactions, and tandem one-pot processes. By integrating mechanistic understanding with catalyst engineering, this review provides a comprehensive perspective and outlines future directions for sustainable, industrially viable closed-loop PET recycling.
